checks: Four real Socket.IO players create, join, ready and start a local room
First snapshot is full for modern and legacy recipients
Small updates use exact decoded deltas; a legacy recipient still receives full state
Control handoff accepts the new actor and bootstraps the old publisher with full state
Stale versions, unauthorized publishers and invalid payloads remain rejected
Deltas contain the server-preserved settings, not the unaccepted publisher variant
A missing baseline rejects the delta, requests full recovery and resumes later deltas
The production receiver rejects corrupt patches and its immutable baseline survives gameplay object mutation
Explicit STATE_REQUEST sends a full snapshot even when a delta baseline exists
A new socket reconnects from a full snapshot and resumes delta updates
Capability negotiation resets on each JOIN_GAME and never sends deltas to legacy clients
A delayed snapshot from another room is ignored without changing the receiver baseline
After all four players opt in, each of three recipients receives exact deltas across five further updates
measurementScope: Deterministic local fixtures with mixed-client compatibility and recovery checks, then five four-modern-player updates; per-message deflate model, not Render billing or observed human gameplay.
